title: Gentleness in all things
hookLine: a man relieves himself in the mosque, the crowd jumps up, and the Prophet asks for a bucket of water

lines: A MAN IN THE MOSQUE CORNER.
cards: A desert Arab walks into the mosque in Medina, goes to a corner, and starts to urinate. On the floor where people pray. The companions leap up, shouting at him to stop.

And the Prophet Muhammad, peace be upon him, says, in Sahih al-Bukhari, in paraphrase: leave him. When he's done, pour a bucket of water over the spot. You were sent to make things easy, not to make them hard.

teach.h: THE FLOOR WASHED, THE MAN KEPT.
teach.b: Look at what the Prophet was protecting. Not the man's behavior: the floor still had to be washed.

In the version in Sahih Muslim, he called the man over afterward and explained, in paraphrase, that mosques aren't for this; they're for remembering Allah, for prayer and recitation. The lesson still got taught.
What he protected was the man, from being chased off in shame, and the people, from turning harsh.
Then the principle. 'A'ishah reports, in Bukhari, in paraphrase: Allah is gentle, and He loves gentleness in all things. Not in some things.
In all of them: correcting someone, raising a child, arguing a point, cleaning up a mess.
In Sahih Muslim she adds, in paraphrase: Allah gives for gentleness what He does not give for harshness.

And: gentleness is not found in anything except that it beautifies it, and it is not taken out of anything except that it spoils it. The Qur'an says something close about the Prophet's own way with people.
In surah Al 'Imran, in paraphrase: it was by mercy from Allah that you were gentle with them; if you had been harsh and hard of heart, they would have scattered from around you.
So rifq isn't weakness, and it isn't letting things slide. The mess was cleaned. The rule was explained.

teach.h: THE HOW, NOT A SOFTER WHAT.
teach.b: Gentleness is the how, not a softer what.

how: Islamic teaching on rifq draws on the hadith that Allah is gentle and loves gentleness in all things, and on the Prophet's gentle handling of the desert Arab in the mosque.

o: a calm, quiet voice kept only for times of prayer
gentleness in how you do things, even when correcting
letting wrongs slide so that nobody ever gets upset

s: the Prophet let the matter go without a word
in Sahih Muslim he called the man over and explained what mosques are for.
the hadith says Allah loves gentleness in all things
'A'ishah, in Bukhari: Allah is gentle and loves gentleness in all things.
the floor was washed and the rule was explained; gentleness is the how.

games.q: a man is urinating in the corner of the mosque, and the companions leap up to stop him. what does the Prophet tell them?
o: tell them to leave him, then pour water over the spot.
rebuke him in front of everyone.
games.why: leave him, pour a bucket of water over it: you were sent to make things easy, not hard (Bukhari). then he explained gently.

practice: Unclench your hands if they're tight, and bring to mind one thing today that tends to come out hard: correcting someone at work, reminding a child for the third time, a text to someone who annoys you.

Run it once in your mind the hard way, then again with rifq, the same message in a slower voice with a softer hand, and notice what changes. If you pray, you can ask Allah, who is gentle, for gentleness.

wordCard.voice: Rifq. Gentleness: the manner of doing anything, so that the truth still gets said and the mess still gets cleaned, without the harshness that spoils it. Today's word.

orig.note: Arabic: gentleness; Allah is described as rafiq, gentle.

carryVoice: Your line: gentle in all things. Same message, softer hand. Go gently.

sources.ref: Sahih al-Bukhari 220 / 6128 (the desert Arab in the mosque: leave him, pour a bucket of water; sent to make things easy)

Sahih Muslim 2593, 2594 (gives for gentleness what He does not give for harshness; gentleness beautifies, its absence spoils)
